ai_summary: Great Britain's wind fleet is currently generating 12.2 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 4.7 GW, representing 46.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This robust renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the GB-wide figure of 132 gCO2/kWh. However, structural transmission bottlenecks across the Scottish-English boundary continue to obstruct the southward flow of this clean electricity. Consequently, 61.9 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £1,621,131. To balance the system and replace this stranded output, thermal plants elsewhere on the network were ramped up, requiring an estimated 11,754,882 m3 of gas to be burned and releasing 21,654 tonnes of additional CO2. Extrapolated across a full year, this equates to an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £592 million. Socialised across national electricity consumption through balancing charges, this ongoing constraint expenditure represents an estimated increase of roughly £2/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the urgent economic and environmental case for expanding cross-border transmission capacity.
